title: Interactive graphics for hierarchical time series
text: aus_tourism data contain quarterly overnight trips 1998 Q1 2022 Q4 76 tourism regions Australia, disaggregated purpose travel. Regions nested within states, purpose travel crossed , gives grouped structure (State / Region) * Purpose. keep vignette small, examples use regions Victoria Tasmania. series every level structure computed aggregate_key(). aggregated series marked <aggregated> key columns. result contains 140 series. total, 2 states 25 regions, taken purposes travel 4 purposes separately.
code: south_east <- aus_tourism[aus_tourism$State %in% c("Victoria", "Tasmania"), ]  tourism_hts <- south_east |>   aggregate_key((State / Region) * Purpose, Trips = sum(Trips)) tourism_hts #> # A tsibble: 14,000 x 5 [1Q] #> # Key:       State, Purpose, Region [140] #> Loading required namespace: crayon #>    Quarter State        Purpose      Region       Trips #>      <qtr> <chr*>       <chr*>       <chr*>       <dbl> #>  1 1998 Q1 <aggregated> <aggregated> <aggregated> 6992. #>  2 1998 Q2 <aggregated> <aggregated> <aggregated> 5489. #>  3 1998 Q3 <aggregated> <aggregated> <aggregated> 4719. #>  4 1998 Q4 <aggregated> <aggregated> <aggregated> 5355. #>  5 1999 Q1 <aggregated> <aggregated> <aggregated> 6230. #>  6 1999 Q2 <aggregated> <aggregated> <aggregated> 5183. #>  7 1999 Q3 <aggregated> <aggregated> <aggregated> 4214. #>  8 1999 Q4 <aggregated> <aggregated> <aggregated> 4793. #>  9 2000 Q1 <aggregated> <aggregated> <aggregated> 6356. #> 10 2000 Q2 <aggregated> <aggregated> <aggregated> 5011. #> # ℹ 13,990 more rows

title: Interactive graphics for hierarchical time series
text: aggregation structure can supplied gig() structure argument added afterwards + hierarchy(). two forms equivalent. hierarchy() object can also created added several plots data.
code: gig(data, structure = (State / Region) * Purpose) + geom_features()  gig(data) + geom_features() + hierarchy((State / Region) * Purpose) tourism_structure <- hierarchy((State / Region) * Purpose) tourism_structure #> <gig_hierarchy> (State/Region)*Purpose #>   keys: State, Region, Purpose

title: Interactive graphics for hierarchical time series
text: feature-space plot displays series one point, positioned two features series. features computed fabletools::features(). feat_stl() gives strength trend seasonality, together several features STL decomposition. x y aesthetics set initial axes. numeric column data can chosen menu either axis. Points coloured level aggregation structure, selecting node hierarchy widget highlights corresponding series.
code: tourism_features <- tourism_hts |>   features(Trips, feat_stl)  gig(   tourism_features,   gig_aes(x = trend_strength, y = seasonal_strength_year) ) +   geom_features() +   tourism_structure

title: Interactive graphics for hierarchical time series
text: STL plot displays observed series together trend, seasonal remainder components. components computed feasts::STL(). trend, seasonality remainder aesthetics must mapped explicitly, component guessed column name. Series different levels structure differ greatly scale. scaled argument geom_stl() accepts second table components computed standardised series, toolbar switches original standardised scale.
code: tourism_stl <- tourism_hts |>   model(stl = STL(Trips)) |>   components()  gig(   tourism_stl,   gig_aes(     x = Quarter, y = Trips, trend = trend,     seasonality = season_year, remainder = remainder   ) ) +   geom_stl() +   tourism_structure tourism_stl_scaled <- tourism_hts |>   group_by_key() |>   dplyr::mutate(Trips = as.numeric(scale(Trips))) |>   dplyr::ungroup() |>   model(stl = STL(Trips)) |>   components()  gig(   tourism_stl,   gig_aes(     x = Quarter, y = Trips, trend = trend,     seasonality = season_year, remainder = remainder   ) ) +   geom_stl(scaled = tourism_stl_scaled) +   tourism_structure

title: Interactive graphics for hierarchical time series
text: sunburst displays aggregation structure . ring corresponds one level structure, segment one node level. table contains key columns aggregated bottom-level series can used, table features computed . Segment labels can switched initially geom_sunburst(labels = FALSE) toggled toolbar.
code: gig(tourism_features) +   geom_sunburst() +   tourism_structure

title: Interactive graphics for hierarchical time series
text: hierarchy widget can also added line plots made plotly::ggplotly() highcharter, add_hierarchy_plotly() add_hierarchy_hc() respectively. plot must identify key values series, described help pages functions. example adds widget highcharter plot.
code: library(highcharter) #> Registered S3 method overwritten by 'quantmod': #>   method            from #>   as.zoo.data.frame zoo #> Highcharts (www.highcharts.com) is a Highsoft software product which is #> not free for commercial and Governmental use  tourism_lines <- data.frame(   Quarter = as.numeric(as.Date(tourism_hts$Quarter)),   State = as.character(tourism_hts$State),   Region = as.character(tourism_hts$Region),   Purpose = as.character(tourism_hts$Purpose),   Trips = tourism_hts$Trips )  highchart() |>   hc_add_series(     tourism_lines,     type = "line",     hcaes(x = Quarter, y = Trips, group = interaction(State, Region, Purpose))   ) |>   add_hierarchy_hc("(State/Region)*Purpose")

what: Saving plots and using them in Shiny
title: Interactive graphics for hierarchical time series
text: gig plot drawn printed. gig_build() returns underlying htmlwidget, can saved standalone web page htmlwidgets::saveWidget(). geom layer pair Shiny functions, geom_featuresOutput() renderGeomFeatures().
code: library(shiny)  ui <- fluidPage(geom_featuresOutput("features", height = "600px"))  server <- function(input, output, session) {   output$features <- renderGeomFeatures(     gig(       tourism_features,       gig_aes(x = trend_strength, y = seasonal_strength_year)     ) +       geom_features() +       tourism_structure   ) }  shinyApp(ui, server)

title: Australian tourism case study
text: Hierarchical time series arise collection series can aggregated along one nested crossed variables. Examples include national, state regional tourism counts, may disaggregated travel purpose. Exploring data requires views respect aggregation structure allow analyst move levels hierarchy. ggelato package provides layered grammar graphics hierarchical time series, modelled design ggplot2. plot created gig(), holds data, aesthetic mapping hierarchical structure, single geometry added +. fridge package coordinates several ggelato plots one interface, selection made one view reflected others. vignette introduces main components grammar using Australian domestic tourism data concludes combining three plots fridge().

title: Australian tourism case study
code: # devtools::install("../fridge") #run this in console # library(fridge) library(ggelato) library(fabletools) library(feasts) library(tsibble) library(dplyr)

title: Australian tourism case study
text: tourism data tsibble package contain quarterly domestic overnight trips Australian regions travel purpose. hierarchical structure (State/Region)*Purpose. means Region nested within State, Purpose crossed State Region. structure imposed fabletools::aggregate_key(), adds aggregate series every level. structure formula passed gig() every plot , ggelato interprets rows data way aggregation.
code: tourism_hts <- tsibble::tourism |>   aggregate_key((State / Region) * Purpose, Trips = sum(Trips))

title: Australian tourism case study
text: Features summarise shape series small number numeric values. feature table computed feasts passed gig(), features interest mapped x y. layer geom_features() draws one point series hierarchy.
code: tourism_ft <- tourism_hts |>   features(Trips, feature_set(pkgs = "feasts"))  tourism_feasts <- gig(tourism_ft,   gig_aes(     x = trend_strength,     y = seasonal_strength_year   ),   structure = (State / Region) * Purpose ) +   geom_features()  tourism_feasts

title: Australian tourism case study
text: decomposition series trend, seasonal remainder components computed upstream fabletools feasts. components mapped channels trend, seasonality remainder, geom_stl() displays series together components. Series different levels hierarchy differ greatly scale. second decomposition therefore computed standardised series supplied scaled argument, allows plot switch original standardised scale.
code: stl_original <- tourism_hts |>   model(stl = STL(Trips)) |>   components()  stl_scaled <- tourism_hts |>   group_by_key() |>   mutate(Trips = as.numeric(scale(Trips))) |>   ungroup() |>   model(stl = STL(Trips)) |>   components() tourism_stl <- gig(   stl_original,   gig_aes(     x = Quarter,     y = Trips,     seasonality = season_year,     trend = trend,     remainder = remainder   ),   structure = (State / Region) * Purpose ) +   geom_stl(scaled = stl_scaled)  tourism_stl
